preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 400 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and isinstance(k, int) and (n & (n - 1) == 0) and 4 <= n <= 2**16 and 0 <= k <= n - 1 for n, k in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is a power of 2 between 4 and 2^16, and k is an integer between 0 and n-1.

preconditions.expression: sum(n for n, k in test_cases) <= 2**16
preconditions.description: The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2^16.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == ['-1'] or (len(output_lines[i]) == n // 2 and all(len(pair) == 2 and isinstance(pair[0], int) and isinstance(pair[1], int) and 0 <= pair[0] < n and 0 <= pair[1] < n and pair[0] != pair[1] for pair in output_lines[i]) and set(x for pair in output_lines[i] for x in pair) == set(range(n)) and sum(pair[0] & pair[1] for pair in output_lines[i]) == k)) for i, output_lines in enumerate(test_outputs))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either -1 (indicating no solution) or a list of n/2 pairs where each pair contains two distinct integers from 0 to n-1, every integer from 0 to n-1 appears exactly once across all pairs, and the sum of bitwise ANDs of the pairs equals k.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == ['-1']) == (not exists_valid_pairing(n, k)) for i, (n, k) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: The output is -1 if and only if no valid pairing exists for the given n and k.
